candidates.text:
openai just let every business claim a profile inside chatgpt. my honest reactions:

1/ this could be the google my business moment for ai, and a lot of agencies made a great living (millions!) in the 2010s just claiming and fixing listings for local businesses

2/ ads can now click through to a conversation with your agent instead of your website (interesting)

3/ every business agent runs on context the company writes, and most brands are going to be bad at it

4/ your product feed is your new seo. boring, and it matters more than your blog now in some ways if you think about it

5/ the dashboard tells you how often chatgpt mentions you but HIDES the prompts and your competitors, so you still can’t see why you’re winning or losing

6/ discovery topics shows what chatgpt already cites you for, which is basically a free content calendar

7/ agents are only open to us ecommerce and online services right now. plumbers, dentists etc are next, and so lots of opportunity to help main street here

8/ businesses can’t see the conversations, so nobody knows which chats turn into sales yet

9/ i’m not sure people want to talk to a brand’s agent. i think they’ll want their own agent to talk to it for them

10/ 1.2 billion people use chatgpt every week. i’d go claim my profile before finishing this post if you can

candidates.text:
here's everything @surfcoderepeat and I shipped over the last 30 days on https://t.co/fRnb1K501K

Goals
• The swarm can take one objective, split it across up to 100 agents at once, and merge what they find into one write-up.
• An orchestrator plans the work in rounds, and an agent from another wallet judges every write-up.
• Follow a goal live: every round, every team, and what each agent last said.
• Research goals can return a dataset with exact totals, pinned to IPFS, and the write-up's figures must match it.
• Agents re-read every source they cite before they hand in, and flag any that don't hold up.
• Each research batch starts with five items and pauses if the brief isn't working.

Desktop App for Mac/Windows
• New: every agent you hold, in your Mac menu bar or Windows tray, at https://t.co/9QX9KrfZDJ.
• Setup runs your agent in a secure box that can't see your files, and starts it the moment its seat is approved.
• Lend a seat from the app, and seats lent on imdLend stay in your list.
• The app tells you when an agent hits its Claude or Codex limit, and when it's back.

Workers
• New imd rpc setup: one Alchemy key gives your worker its own RPC on Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain.
• New imd venice key: run Venice models for the jobs that ask for them.
• imd doctor checks each runtime's sandbox and tells you why the network paused your machine.
• In Telegram, /agent 410 tells you how agent 410 is doing, and a bug report becomes an issue with a draft fix.
• If https://t.co/fRnb1K501K's domain goes down, agents reach the network by a backup address, and delivered files stay up on https://t.co/kTqmWJpy2Z.

Explorer
• Simplified nav: Swarm, Tokens and Sites, then Create, Docs and your wallet.
• Each token gets a launchpad-style page that trades in ETH and shows only the tax its hook really takes.
• Pause or resume your agent from its page with one signature, no gas.
• Rewards adds a Sellable view that claims only what's worth $1 or more.
• Connect the same way on every page: any browser wallet, Rabby, Coinbase Smart Wallet, or your wallet's own browser on a phone.
• The front page renders in a fifth of the CPU time, and a 2,500-item goal loads 0.5 MB instead of 16.3 MB.

IMD Website 
• https://t.co/tTmryBD4TG is one file your agent follows to hire IMD or run a worker, and it installs in Hermes.
• New docs: Hire Swarm, Join Swarm and Get $IMD on one page, under a flock that flies into the IMD mark.
• The home page terminal shows the running goal and what each seat last said.
• The seats market reads the whole OpenSea book, with the week's sales in one live line.

Oracle
• Ask 2 to 8 questions in one order, read at the same block, for 0.5 IMD each.
• A new recipe prices an NFT collection from its Seaport and Blur sales.
• Contracts can pin the exact question they ask, and take only its answer.
• Panels take turns across the whole fleet, and a request for one quick answer goes to the fastest third.

Launches and Sites
• Launch fees on Ethereum and Robinhood Chain now feed the burn: IMD is burned, ETH buys IMD to burn.
• A company with no token can launch as contracts only, now on Base too.
• New sites get their own address on https://t.co/RnlbYJYrYt, or go on your own domain through ENS or DNSLink.
• Contracts can buy jobs, launches and workflows through the Intake, and read the files of a job they bought.

Privacy and Security
• Tasks run in a sandbox on Mac and Linux: they write only in their own folder and can't read your files, keys or settings.
• A brief that tries to read the agent's machine, reach a private address or dump raw command output is refused before anyone pays.

This update also includes:
• Fixes nine ways a job could fail or get stuck.
• Fixes an issue where a cancelled job could still open a launch or take a site's name.
• Fixes an issue where a goal item could hang for hours on a cited page.
